backlog.spec: In solve, record the CPU time of each restart (SLSQP plus repair) and keep the maximum seen so far, t_max. Replace the loop condition with: elapsed + 1.3*t_max < 0.9*time_limit. Before the first restart, t_max is 0. Set the guided-phase threshold to half of 0.9*time_limit. This uses the time the 0.8 fraction now wastes, while staying well under the 45 s void limit. Remove TIME_FRACTION, or set it to 0.9 and use it in both places.
backlog.title: Budget-aware stop instead of a fixed 80 percent

backlog.spec: Guided restarts currently jitter every centre by N(0, 0.03). Pass the incumbent radii to _solve_once with the incumbent centres. Set the jitter sd for circle i to 0.012 + 0.05*(1 - r_i/r_max), where r_max is the largest incumbent radius. Small circles, which are often rattlers or badly placed, then move a lot. The large circles that carry most of the sum barely move. Clip to [0, 1] as now. The starting radii stay at INIT_RADIUS.
backlog.title: Radius-dependent jitter for guided restarts

backlog.spec: Maintain a small pool of the best k=5 distinct packings found so far (sorted by radius sum). Each restart either creates a fresh random packing or perturbs a randomly chosen pool member; after each SLSQP solve, insert the result into the pool if it beats the worst member and is not a duplicate in radius sum. Return the best member after repair.
backlog.title: Keep the top-k packings and polish all of them

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, pass analytic gradients to SLSQP. Objective jac: zeros for the 2n centre entries and -1 for the n radius entries. Constraint jac: build a dense (m, 3n) matrix. For pair row k=(i,j), set dc_i = (c_i-c_j)/d_ij (guard d with max(d,1e-12)), dc_j = -dc_i, dr_i = dr_j = -1. Wall rows get ±1 on the matching coordinate and -1 on r. The r>=0 rows get +1. Compute the static parts once outside the closure and fill in only the pair rows on each call. Pass the matrix as constraints={'type':'ineq','fun':cons,'jac':cons_jac}. Results stay the same, but each restart runs much faster than with finite differences, so more restarts fit in the time.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Initialise radii heterogeneously: draw radii from uniform [0.03, 0.12] for each circle and centres by Poisson-disc-like rejection sampling, so that big and small circles mix. Optimal packings for this problem have mixed radii, so this starts nearer to those basins.
backlog.title: Sorted-radius diversity init

backlog.spec: Raise MAX_ITER from 200 to 1000 and pass options ftol=1e-12 (and disp=False) to SLSQP so that each local solve converges more tightly before the repair step. Also lower INIT_RADIUS to 0.01 so the initial configuration is less overlapping and SLSQP starts from a more feasible point.
backlog.title: Increase the iteration cap and convergence tolerance

backlog.spec: Keep the current guided-restart logic unchanged. For non-guided restarts only (init is None), add a first SLSQP stage before the free-radius stage. Its variables are the 2n centres plus one shared radius R, with objective -R and constraints: pairwise distance >= 2R, and every centre within [R, 1-R] on each axis. Start from the uniform random centres with R=0.03 and use maxiter=100. Then start the existing free-radius SLSQP from the resulting centres, with every radius set to R. Guided restarts skip the pre-stage and behave exactly as now. This repeats slot 27, which scored -2.9396 without slot 1, on top of the current incumbent.
backlog.title: Stack equal-radius pre-stage on the guided incumbent

backlog.spec: Replace _repair. After SLSQP, clip the centres to [0,1] and solve scipy.optimize.linprog for the radii with the centres held fixed: maximise sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs, 0 <= r_i <= min(x_i, y_i, 1-x_i, 1-y_i), method='highs'. Subtract 1e-12 from every d_ij and wall bound so the result passes the 1e-10 check. Then run a final check: if any overlap remains, scale the offending radii down as the current loop does. The result is the best radii for the given centres, never worse than the greedy repair.
backlog.title: LP-optimal radii instead of greedy repair

backlog.spec: For non-guided restarts, initialise radii as uniform(0.02, 0.08) per circle instead of the constant INIT_RADIUS. Guided restarts keep the constant. This gives SLSQP a size mixture to begin with.
backlog.title: Random initial radii in non-guided starts

backlog.spec: Use the main loop until 0.75*time_limit. Then run one more SLSQP on the best packing, starting exactly from its centres and radii with no jitter, with options maxiter=1000 and ftol=1e-15. Repair and keep it only if the sum is larger. Also set TIME_FRACTION so that the polish finishes within about 0.9*time_limit: check process_time before starting and skip the polish if more than 0.85*time_limit has been used. This removes the slack that SLSQP leaves at its default ftol 1e-6.
backlog.title: Final high-precision polish of best

backlog.spec: Set SHRINK to 2e-10 in the repair step. Check that the final packing is still valid by verifying the pairwise overlap and the wall constraint in double precision after the repair. If it is not, subtract 1e-9 from the radii again. The gain is about 3e-8 per circle, so this is a cheap test of the safety margin.
backlog.title: Remove clip and use a tighter SHRINK

backlog.spec: Keep a list of the 3 best distinct repaired packings (distinct if the sums differ by more than 1e-6). A guided restart picks one of them uniformly at random as its init. Non-guided restarts and the final return of the best are unchanged.
backlog.title: Guided restarts start from pool of top 3 incumbents

backlog.spec: For a guided restart, with probability 0.5 (seed rng), before the usual jitter, swap the centres of two circles of the incumbent whose radii differ by more than 20 percent. Pick the pair uniformly among such pairs. Then start SLSQP with radii set to the incumbent radii permuted the same way, which keeps radius i with its new centre. Shrink those starting radii by a factor of 0.95 so the start is nearly feasible, and use jitter sd 0.01 instead of 0.03. This explores different size assignments within the same contact structure. The other half of guided restarts are unchanged.
backlog.title: Position-swap move in guided restarts

backlog.spec: For guided restarts, instead of jittering every centre by the same normal(0, 0.03), jitter only the circles whose incumbent radius is in the smallest half (by radius). Those centres get rng.normal(0, 0.05), the larger circles get rng.normal(0, 0.005). Implement this inside _solve_once's init branch by computing a per-circle sigma from the incumbent radii, which requires passing the incumbent radii alongside the centres. Everything else is unchanged.
backlog.title: Small-circle-targeted jitter for guided starts

backlog.spec: For guided restarts in the second half of the budget, with probability 0.25, keep the incumbent centres exactly (no jitter) and instead redraw the starting radii as rng.uniform(0.02, 0.08, n), so SLSQP starts from the same packing with a fresh radius profile. Otherwise use the existing guided jitter. The radius-only start tests whether the radius assignment alone can move the incumbent to a better local optimum.
backlog.title: Radii-only kick from incumbent centres

backlog.spec: In solve, make the guided-restart jitter scale depend on elapsed time instead of the fixed 0.03. Let frac be the fraction of the guided phase elapsed, from 0 at the start of the guided phase to 1 at the end, and set sigma = 0.05 * (0.1 ** frac). Pass sigma into _solve_once as an argument used in place of the literal 0.03 in rng.normal(0, 0.03, ...). Non-guided restarts keep sigma unused. The guided search is then broad early and fine-grained late.
backlog.title: Decaying guided jitter scale

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when init is given, replace the fixed jitter sd of 0.03 with a scale drawn for each restart from the seed rng. Use sigma = exp(rng.uniform(log(0.005), log(0.06))) and apply it as rng.normal(0, sigma, (n, 2)) before the clip. Some guided restarts then make fine local refinements and others make larger basin hops. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Log-uniform guided jitter scale

backlog.spec: Replace the single SLSQP call by a two-stage solve: first optimise a smooth penalty objective (negative radius sum plus a quadratic penalty on overlaps and boundary violations, penalty weight increasing 10 to 1e6 across stages) using L-BFGS-B, then polish the result with SLSQP on the exact constraints. This gives a better-conditioned start for SLSQP and typically finds denser packings.
backlog.title: Two-stage optimisation with a penalty continuation

backlog.spec: Replace uniform random init with perturbed hexagonal-like layouts: choose random row counts (e.g. 5-6 rows with 5-7 circles per row totalling 32, randomly chosen), place centres on staggered rows, add gaussian jitter sd ~0.02, and set initial radii to ~0.08. Mix 50% structured starts with 50% random ones.
backlog.title: Structured initial layouts (hex/grid rows)

backlog.spec: Pass a max-iteration argument to _solve_once: 200 for random starts, 400 for guided restarts, because guided starts are near a good optimum and can profit from fully converging. Use the argument in the minimize options.
backlog.title: Higher SLSQP iteration cap for guided restarts

backlog.spec: Replace the argmax-driven loop in _repair with a sweep: for each of up to 50 passes, visit all pairs (i, j) with i < j in a random order drawn from the seed's rng (pass the rng into _repair), and for each violating pair scale both radii by d/(r_i+r_j). Stop when a full pass has no violation. Pass rng through from solve so all randomness still comes from the seed. The overlap-removal path is different, which may shrink the radii less on average.
backlog.title: Random-order pair sweep in the repair step

backlog.spec: Set INIT_RADIUS to 0.03 for non-guided restarts (the guided ones keep 0.05). Smaller starting radii give SLSQP feasible starting points with fewer violated constraints, which may converge in fewer iterations and allow more restarts.
backlog.title: Smaller initial radius for non-guided starts

backlog.spec: Supply jac for the objective (gradient: zeros for centres, -1 for radii) and a vectorized analytic Jacobian for the constraint function (pairwise distance rows with sparse-like dense fill, boundary rows, radius rows). This speeds each SLSQP iteration a lot, so many more restarts fit in 30 s. Keep the constraint ordering identical to cons.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when init is not None, draw the jitter sd per call as exp(uniform(log 0.005, log 0.08)) from rng instead of the fixed 0.03. This mixes fine and coarse perturbations of the incumbent. Leave the rest unchanged.
backlog.title: Guided jitter sigma randomised log-uniformly

backlog.spec: Initialise radii with a random mix: draw each initial radius from a uniform distribution on [0.02, 0.12] instead of a constant INIT_RADIUS, so the first SLSQP step starts with heterogeneous circle sizes that the optimiser can sort out. This encourages the varied-radius structures that maximise the radius sum for unequal circles.
backlog.title: Dynamic circle-count mixing of radius sizes

backlog.spec: In guided restarts, in addition to the jitter, pick two circles with clearly different radii (ratio over 1.3) in the incumbent and swap their centres. Initial radii are the incumbent radii times 0.9, swapped likewise. This tests size-position permutations that SLSQP cannot reach by itself.
backlog.title: Swap-two-circles kick in guided restarts

backlog.spec: In solve, change the guided condition. Guided restarts become possible once elapsed time exceeds 0.3*TIME_FRACTION*time_limit, instead of 0.5. Once possible, a restart is guided with probability 0.65 instead of 0.5. Define these as two module constants, GUIDED_START=0.3 and GUIDED_PROB=0.65, and change nothing else.
backlog.title: Earlier and more frequent guided restarts

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP in _solve_once, run scipy L-BFGS-B on the unconstrained penalty function f(v) = -sum r + mu*(sum relu(r_i+r_j-d_ij)^2 + sum relu(r-x)^2 + relu(r-y)^2 + relu(x+r-1)^2 + relu(y+r-1)^2), with an analytic numpy gradient. Use bounds centres in [0,1] and r in [0,0.5]. Run it for mu in [10, 100, 1000, 1e4], warm-starting each stage from the last, with maxiter 200 each. Then pass the result as x0 to SLSQP. The pre-solve is cheap, so SLSQP starts close to feasible and converges in few iterations, which allows more restarts.
backlog.title: Penalty L-BFGS-B pre-solve then SLSQP

backlog.spec: Only include pair constraints for pairs whose centre distance is below 0.35 at the start of each SLSQP call (re-evaluated in a second call from the result). This cuts the constraint count from 496 to about 150, speeding SLSQP considerably. Finish with a full-constraint run to ensure validity.
backlog.title: Two-stage SLSQP with active pair constraints

backlog.spec: In guided restarts, add jitter (sd 0.08) only to circles whose centres lie within a random radius (0.2 to 0.4) of a random point in the square. Other circles get a jitter of sd 0.005. Radii start at INIT_RADIUS. This is a local-neighbourhood kick instead of a global one.
backlog.title: Guided restarts: perturb only a random disc region

memo: Helped: only slot 1 (guided restarts in the second half, half start from the best packing), -2.9365, delta -0.0112. It is a single run and noise sd is about 0.0034, so it is unconfirmed. Not helped: nearly everything else, mostly within noise. That covers new initialisations (2, 9, 18, 29, 34), crossover (3), penalty or barrier solvers (4, 24), analytic gradients (5), gravity (10), pair pruning (11), successive halving (19), population/Metropolis schemes (20, 23), and post-polish steps (16, 28, 31, 33). Near misses, run without slot 1: 21 (-2.9396), 27 (-2.9396), 6 (-2.9386), 17 (-2.9380).
